claims.text: A secondary controlled heating step drives a nanoframework phase transformation in Pt–Ru-based HEA nanomaterials.
The phase transformation organizes the alloy components into a high-density, catalytically active architecture.
Precise variation of Pt–Ru composition mediates structural reorganization.
Structural reorganization governs reliable formation of the HEA phase.
Structural reorganization governs enhanced catalytic performance.
Precursors obtained after the initial spray-drying and thermal decomposition-reduction step are disordered mixed-metal nanoparticles.
The initial precursors have a broadly distributed Pt–Ru ratio.
A controlled inert or mildly reducing atmosphere and a narrow secondary-heating temperature range promote the proposed phase transformation.
Avoiding overheating improves reproducibility of the nanoframework structure.
The resulting nanoframework has increased grain-boundary density.
The resulting nanoframework contains ordered Pt–Ru bonding configurations.
Secondary heating facilitates controlled diffusion and rearrangement of metal atoms.
Atomic diffusion and rearrangement transform the material from a disordered state to a more ordered nanoframework.
Nanoframework reorganization increases the density of catalytic active sites.
Nanoframework reorganization improves charge-transfer characteristics.
Increased active-site density and improved charge transfer enhance catalytic performance.
Relative to an unheated baseline, secondary-heated material will exhibit more uniform nanoscale ordering.
Relative to an unheated baseline, secondary-heated material will have a higher density of catalytically active interfaces.
Relative to an unheated baseline, secondary-heated material will show higher catalytic activity or selectivity.
Prior observations in similar systems support a role for secondary heating in phase transformation.
